children: KPMG Canada confirmed on Wednesday a third party gained unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents in a cybersecurity incident.
The firm did not disclose how many clients were affected, how many files were compromised or how the breach occurred.
KPMG has secured its systems and is contacting affected clients, spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth said.

"We are confident we have protected our clients' information and, based on our ongoing monitoring, the information impacted by this incident is not available online or being misused for any purpose," Cloutier-Bosworth said.
The Globe and Mail first reported the news earlier in the day.

The incident comes amid heightened cyber risks for professional-service and financial firms that hold sensitive client information. Recent attacks have targeted law firms, private equity firms and other financial companies.
